business_summary: MasTec, Inc. is a Florida-headquartered, NYSE-listed infrastructure construction company operating through Communications, Clean Energy and Infrastructure, Power Delivery, and Pipeline Infrastructure segments. Its Power Delivery segment builds and upgrades electric transmission lines, substations and distribution infrastructure for utility customers; that segment is the mapped grid-interconnect exposure. The company's other segments (communications, pipeline, clean energy generation) sit outside the mapped chain.

exposure_summary.narrative: MasTec sits on grid-interconnect, scored UNDISCOVERED. Its second-quarter 2026 release reports Power Delivery revenue up nearly 20% year over year with EBITDA growth of 24% and a record segment backlog of $6.3 billion, up nearly $1.3 billion year over year, driven by utility transmission, substation and reliability spending that management explicitly ties to demand from mission-critical infrastructure requiring grid expansion.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: MasTec discloses Power Delivery segment revenue growth (approximately 20% year over year) and segment backlog ($6.3 billion) but not a data-center-specific revenue percentage; Power Delivery serves broad utility transmission and reliability demand, of which data-center-driven load growth is one named but unquantified driver, per the located second-quarter 2026 release.

implied_fcf_cagr.basis: Free-cash-flow CAGR the current enterprise value 24081658756.0 implies over a 5-year explicit period on base FCF 474004000, solved by bisection at a 0.09 discount rate and 0.025 terminal growth. Assumption-dependent expectation reading, not a reported figure.

horizon_spread.basis: Spread between the implied CAGR solved over the shortest and longest explicit periods (5y: 0.3229, 7y: 0.2392, 10y: 0.1802) in quality.reverse_dcf.implied_by_horizon; inherits the same assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

crowdedness_caveats: The grid-interconnect link is scored UNDISCOVERED at crowdedness 30, the chain's lowest retail-attention reading, though its capture score (40) is explicitly named as the chain's TRAP EXAMPLE: much of the link is regulated-return or competitively bid EPC, meaning volume growth does not automatically convert to proportional profit capture.

MasTec's own capture on this link is a construction-services margin (EBITDA growth of 24% against revenue growth of nearly 20% in Power Delivery in Q2 2026 per the located release), which is closer to the capped-capture pattern the chain's rationale describes than to a product manufacturer's pricing power.

data/market/MTZ.json carries no pcs (positioning/crowdedness-signal) block, so this profile cannot independently corroborate the link-level crowdedness score with issuer-level analyst-coverage or institutional-ownership figures.
